subject.title: Write tool lacks append mode — isolated cron sessions destroy shared files

question: Should OpenClaw add append support to the existing `write` tool API for ordinary agent and cron runs, or require a different append primitive?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the remaining choice is a model-facing core tool contract and the open implementation PR is conflicting, so automation should not invent the permanent API shape.

options.title: Land append on `write`
options.body: Rebase and review the linked PR or equivalent implementation that adds a backwards-compatible append option while preserving overwrite as the default.

options.title: Choose a separate append primitive
options.body: Ask for a dedicated append tool or `mode` design before continuing the linked PR, trading more API surface for clearer operation naming.

options.title: Defer core API
options.body: Document backup and `exec >>` workarounds for trusted operators, accepting that ordinary cron and agent writes can still truncate append-intent files.

recommendation.title: Land append on `write`
recommendation.body: Rebase and review the linked PR or equivalent implementation that adds a backwards-compatible append option while preserving overwrite as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest file-tool history signal and are the best available owner for a core tool-contract direction choice.
